title: Uber Just Gave 30,000 Employees an AI Agent
content:
Uber just gave an AI agent to more than thirty thousand employees.
And the most interesting part is how they got there.
On October twenty second, Uber announced a company-wide rollout of ChatGPT Work, an agent inside ChatGPT Enterprise.
It connects to tools like Gmail, Google Drive, Google Calendar and Slack.
Employees can research, prepare meeting briefs, build presentations and analyze data.
But they did NOT start with thirty thousand people.
They started with a pilot of one thousand employees.
Here is the detail I find most useful.
Uber's VP of engineering told TechCrunch that around eighty percent of the pilot users were non-engineers.
People in finance, operations and product used it to analyze data, localize training materials and build their own dashboards.
And there is one more idea worth stealing.
Earlier this year, Uber paired thirty AI engineers with teams across the company, and gave them two weeks to automate key parts of their jobs.
They called these AI pods.
Technical skill plus deep knowledge of the job. That combination is where the value showed up.
So how can a smaller company use this playbook?
Step one. Start with a small pilot, not the whole company.
Step two. Pair one technical person with the team that owns the work.
Step three. Build a small library of approved prompts and integrations, which Uber calls its internal AI skills library.
Step four. Train people before you scale.
Step five. Measure what changed. Uber says it will track how employees use the tool and what workflows they create.
Imagine a fifty person agency doing this with five people for one month. You would learn more than from a year of debating.
Here's my take. Uber did not disclose the cost, and the results are still to come, so this is not proof yet.
But the method is right. Adoption is not a software purchase. It is a change in how people work.
And the person who can sit between the team and the technology is going to be very valuable.
